item.title: Choshim
item.dc:creator: acoke4u
item.content:encoded:
I remember when I asked my uncle, who is a renown scientist in his field, how he is successful in research and publishing.
“You have to know just a little less,” he said. And it struck me where I was looking for answers.
After going through most of your career having seen the complexities, understanding the procedures it takes to get to a certain mastery level, it all becomes obvious and mundane. Yeah, If I want to do research on this topic, I know I have to do the literature review plan out the experiment, then execute it and write a paper for publication. Then repeat. Or, if I want to start a project or a business, I do my research, I execute and evaluate the outcome. The process still feels the same.
What I felt that I was missing in this process was what my uncle was able to highlight for me. If you think you know it all, there will be no questions to ask. By knowing just a little less about the world, he meant that you will preserve that innocent curiosity that will drive you do continue your work, even if you maybe going through the same physically and mentally steps.
That innocence, newness, or beginner’s mind is called Choshim (초심) in Korean (based on Chinese characters 初心 – composed of the characters ‘beginning/initial’ and ‘heart/mind’). In fact, it reminds me of an excerpt I read about Picasso’s work and how he later pursued child-like art that is untutored, untrained, unrestrained. He was quoted saying,
“Every child is an artist. The problem is how to remain an artist once we grow up.”
It is so easy to mindlessly go through the repetitive things I do in life. But I think it’s important to remind ourselves to retain Choshim, a goal I will try to achieve throughout the site.

item.title: Just Enjoy It
item.dc:creator: acoke4u
item.content:encoded: I admit. I am one of those people who seldom follow through with my ideas. My hobbies are always in flux, and short-ended,  most of which would not even be pursued long-enough to be even considered a hobby – more like an interest of the month. Yeah, I can say it’s because I don’t have time, or energy, or because of a million other reasons. But really, I’m afraid. I’m afraid it won’t be good enough, it won’t be successful, it won’t be unique, and so on. In the end, I end up pursuing nothing. I’ve worked hard to get this point where I can pursue a serious hobby. Now that I am here, it’s like trying to choose toothpaste amongst the overwhelming number of brands at a grocery store. I am paralyzed by freedom (or in this case capitalism). It wasn’t until I started reading Elizabeth Gilbert’s book “Big Magic”  that I realized, first, its not an uncommon struggle, and second, there are other ways to think about pursuing your creative side.  She essentially reminded me that the creative process is happiness in itself. Who cares about whether it’s successful, or recognized, or any other value society puts to your pursuit. Go for it because it balances your life and brings value to it, and because you’re inspired by it and have your heart and soul in it. Being a driven person, it was a nice reminder that sometimes you do things out of your intrinsic happiness even if it may not be up anything to society. I think I have put a lot of pressure on myself to pursue a useful hobby, to spend my time efficiently, and to make it perfect. But in the end, it only seems to have prevented me from enjoying my interest,  not to mention even starting one. So, I’m going to just enjoy it from now on. And if my hobbies turn into something productive to the world, great. If not, that’s ok, too, because it made a difference in my life.

item.title: 2016 Resolution #1
item.dc:creator: acoke4u
item.content:encoded: #1. More Laughter in my life At some point we all lose our child-like innocence. Life becomes stale and redundant and no longer playing house in a cardboard box feels like that imaginary kingdom. Remember that excitement buying your first nintendo system? (thanks dad, I will always remember you). I spent hours venturing into the new world that I unboxed. Somewhere in my life I lost that excitement. Maybe I was a serious child from the start. I was always too pensive for my age. Even now I feel like an old-soul. And I guess, although I hate to admit, I am stoic and serious at work (but easy-going). We’re all a blend of characteristics. Like finely aged-wine, I’m have an easy-going base with overtones of seriousness and moments of excitement and laughter. (What is your wine personality?) Maybe it’s the work I do or just working in general. My job requires that I am serious and responsible. It augments the serious overtones in my personality, and like aged-wine it has solidified them well. But hey I need some laughter in my life. After all, it is the year of the monkey – what better way to spend 2016 with laughter?

item.title: 2016 Resolution #2
item.dc:creator: acoke4u
item.content:encoded:
#2 Work for it

I love short cuts. If I can put in less time and energy to complete a task, I’m all about it. Nowadays, we are surrounded by these quick and easy tools. I can take a picture of my food and in seconds, boom done – ive just shared it with the world.

But I’m thinking there are just certain things that requires you to take the long and tedious road. Because maybe we think we want to achieve a goal but the matter of fact is we need to go through the process of getting there. And it actually requires a bit of effort – shocker.

It’s come to my realization that even exploring what to do next in itself requires a significant amount of work. Especially if you have all the freedom and no institution or other external factors motivating you to hit a deadline. It’s just me and myself, and the endless possibilities. And it’s rather unsettling.

With freedom, you have to be even more motivated and diligent to get things done. Whether it is working out, finding your hobbies, connecting with friends. No longer is someone telling you what to do and making you accountable with deadlines.

The world is nothing but chaos, and we find meaning from it through our efforts.

item.title: Summary: Big Magic (E. Gilbert)
item.dc:creator: acoke4u
item.content:encoded:
My notes on Big Magic by Elizabeth Gilbert:
  • Ideas are a living force
    • Ideas are driven to be made manifest either by you or someone else
    • Sometimes it's not the right time when you have an idea - it's ok to move on.
    • Someone else might have the same idea but were the ones to follow through with it - and that's ok.
  • Follow your curiosity and remain open. Have a sense of wonder.
    • Acknowledge your fears but don't let it lead your creative life.
    • Let your ego serve you instead of it controlling you.
  • Your art does not have to be original. It does not have to be important, and it does not have to be perfect.
    • "Done is better than good." - Big Magic
    • It's never too late.
    • "If you argue for your limitations you get to keep them. But if you argue for your possibilities,you get to create them." - Kelly Lee Phipps
    • All ideas have already been done before, but it has not been done by you.
    • Approach with a stubborn gladness
    • "What will make you finish is not self-discipline, but self-forgiveness" - Liz Gilbert
  • Is it worth it in the end?
    • Every endeavor has its downfalls. It's a matter of what you do is worth dealing with the negative aspects that come with it.
    • When you're stuck try Combinatory play - the act of opening up one mental channel through something else.
  • Live in your own creative world away from what other people think
    • "It ain't what they call you; it's what you answer to." - WC Fields
My thoughts: Absolutely adored the book and is one that I would keep in my bookshelf to re-read. E Gilbert has a refreshing way of inspiring others to follow their passion. Through her witty writing, her book focuses on the creative process and its struggles which have not been clearly addressed before.

item.title: Quotes: The Walk (2015)
item.dc:creator: acoke4u
item.content:encoded:
My collection of memorable quotes from The Walk (2015)
  • Why do you walk on the wire? Why do you tempt fate? Why do you chase...DEATH? But I do not think of it this way. LIFE! For me, walking on the wire...is life. C'est la vie.
  • No matter where I was going, or what I was doing... I was always searching for the perfect place to hang my rope.
  • It looks so... Beautiful, yes... And dangerous. And completely insane... And you are a madman. [Yes, I am mad. But it's my dream.] Then if it is your dream, you must do it.
  • Most wire walkers, they die when they arrive. They think they have arrived... But they are still on the wire. If  you have three steps to do, and if you do those steps arrogantly... if you think you are invincible... you are going to die! Tu vas mourir.
  • Now I know what the void is... I'm a wire-walker. The void is my domain. But not this void. But somehow I gather the strength to whisper... whisper so the demons won't hear...It's impossible... But i'll do it.
  • You cannot lie on stage. The audience will always feel what is inside your heart.
  • Annie, my head is full of... doubts. When it comes time for me to step on the wire... to confront the void. I'm not sure I'll be able to make the first step. [You're heart will tell you what to do. Your accomplices...and your towers will be there to support you.]
  • The dressing room is where the transformation takes place...where the disguised impostor...the intruder... Becomes the performer. The artist.
  • Before I took that first step, I felt that Jeff no longer existed. My tower was deserted. I felt that the horizon was no longer pat of what we call "the rotundity of the earth." The wire was a floating line to infinity. I no longer heard the sounds of New York. Everything fell silent. I was about to step into an unknown world... "The Void."
  • The moment my entire weight is on that wire, I feel immediately a feeling that I know by heart... I feel the wire... I feel the support of the Towers.
  • I was walking across a beautiful sea of unknown dimension. Gravity did not exist. I was among the clouds.
  • And I arrive at the North Tower feeling the most immense elation... The most intense joy that I ever felt in my life.
  • I'm going to remain there an eternity, drinking that void...and being called by the Towers to dance on that wire. And I remember being overcome by the most profound feeling of awareness, of consciousness...of gratitude.
  • I salute the Towers. And the wire, and my accomplices...and of course, I salute New York. And I'm so taken with my emotions... I had completely forgotten, this is actually a performance.
  • I look down... And it was... It was beautiful. I was calm and beautiful, and serene, and "not-dangerous".
  • I cannot end this walk with a feeling of dishonor...Feeling as if I've been assailed by the gods. No, I will only leave my magnificent wire, and my beautiful towers... With my head held high.
  • [Why did you do this?] There is no "why." Just because... When I see a beautiful place to put my wire, I cannot resist.
My thoughts: Truly inspirational story that leaves you with the courage to live your dreams. The movie brings Philip's dreams to the mainstream audience, allowing us to share in his journey. The original documentary warrants a watch for those looking for more.

item.title: A Blinking Cursor
item.dc:creator: acoke4u
item.content:encoded:
One of the more anxiety-provoking moments is a blinking cursor. It doesn't quite tell you what to be afraid of outright, but like a Japanese horror film, it has a subtle way of nagging your insides. Nagging at the fact that you have a blank screen, provoking anxiety knowing the possibilities are limitless. 'Cuz the freedom comes without rules, and highly depends on your own creative mind, your own set of rules that you've established. And dare you express your voice.
It fights against what you're expected to do, or what you think you're expected to do. The outside pressures unconsciously or consciously soften your own voice to creativity, to originality. And what a hard task it is to follow that small voice.
When you find it and follow it, however, it's powerful. It's the power core to Iron man - it is the essence of what makes him super, and you fabulous. You no longer want to stray from your own voice because it felt just right, at ease, and a quiet confidence brews. It becomes easier and easier to find that voice and the follow it, and you just become yourself. And the world needs you.
So create, go wild with that blinking cursor. Dare to express yourself.

item.title: If You Can: How Millennials Can Get Rich Slowly (Bernstein)
item.dc:creator: acoke4u
item.content:encoded:
• Traditional pension plans of our parent's age are disappearing, so need to invest well
Hurdle 1 - Be frugal
Hurdle 2 - Learn about finances - read financial books/blogs
  • Real Return - Think in terms of Real return on your savings by taking into account inflation (about 2%)
    • ex: 5% return on savings - 2% inflation = 3% real return on investments
    • Should technically invest monthly adjusting for inflation also ($100, $102, etc) but income should be adjusting for inflation anyways so just invest a % instead of fixed amount
  • Stock - sell ownership interest
    • No one can predict the market short-term but long-term it's steady
  • Bond - borrowed money
    • W/ profit, you pay off lenders first and after excluding expenses of the business, you pay off residual owners of the stock
    • B/c lenders of bonds are risk averse they don't get to vote on company board (but stock holders do b/c they want to maximize profits)
    • --> thus corporate bonds generally bad deal, should confine to gov offerings
  • Investing assets 
    • high risk ones but potentially high returns - like stocks
    • low risk ones w low returns - T bills, CDs, money market funds
  • Example
    • Treasury bonds - ~3.6% yield over 30 years w 1.4% yield after inflation-adjustment (-2%)
    • Domestic stocks - 2% yield + growth rate 1.5%
    • Thus 2/3 stocks, 1/3 bonds = ~3% return long-term
    • Spreadsheet of accumulated assets over time : www.efficientfrontier.com/files/savings-path.xls
  • Consider vanguard group - you own shares vs other mutual companies
Hurdle 3 - Learn about financial history (nothing is new, so understand where you fit in history of marketing/finance)
  • If economy is bad, future returns are high, vice versa
    • If friends recommend stock, or investment/real estate, may you shouldn't be whereas if they respond negatively to your investment strategy may it's a good sign
  • Still can't Time the market despite this
    • use knowledge of financial history as emotional stabilizer to keep portfolio even keel and prevent you from going all-in to the market when everyone else is too or selling when economy is bad
    • Allows discipline of sticking to fixed stock/bond allocation and sell at high prices and buy at low ones
Hurdle 4 - Maintain strict long-term discipline in saving and investing
  • Know yourself and fight against messing up your portfolio for short-term gains
Hurdle 5 - Assume everyone is giving you bad advice (dont listen to the chatter), and choose your advisors very carefully
  • Avoid any stock broker, full-service brokerage firm, newsletter, adviser who purchases individual securities, hedge fund, most mutual fund companies, most financial advisors
    • stock brokers do not need to comply w fiduciary duty (vs advisor)- can be your friends, relatives so deflect any conversation
  • Mutual fund industry lightly less hostile
    • due to 1940 Investment Company Act
    • but primarily focus on growing their funds (AUMs) (not your returns) although tighter linkage b/w two compared to brokerage
    • mutual fund or brokerage company has 2 owners = clients who buy mutual funds/stocks/bonds and shareholders who own stock of company itself
    • fund companies raise fund fees but you're unlikely to notice its effect for many years
    • except vanguard (has one owner)
    • you get charged more in fees than expense ratio which exceeded by transnational costs
HOW TO
  • Steps
    • Max out employer match in 401k regardless of loans (return >50%)
    • Eliminate debt
      1. Credit card --> car loan --> student loans
    • Establish emergency fund
    • Establish emergency fund
      1. = 6 months living expenses in a taxable account
      2. T bills, CDs, money market accounts
    • Only then can you start saving for retirement (IRA, 401k, taxable accounts) = at least 15% of your income
      • Max out 401k match --> max out Roth IRA --> save in taxable account on top of that
      • In your contributions to 401k, IRA, taxable accounts - equally distribute b/w US stock, foreign stock, bond funds --> rebalance one a year
        • in good years sell some stocks - but avoid in taxable account since incur capital gains taxes
        • which means keeping stock holdings in a tax sheltered 401k or IRA
      • Index funds to use
        • vanguard funds, US total stock market index fund, Total international stock index fund, Short-term Bond index or Total bond market index fund, Or fidelity spartan series (total market index, international index, US bond index or short-term treasury bond index funds)
      • can slice/dice US and foreign stock options in smaller pieces (REITs, emerging/developed markets for foreign stocks)
      • more 401k are making "target funds"
        • ex: vanguard has target retirement funds - fees 0.16%-0.18%. 2060 fund had 90% stock which falls each %/year as person gets older
  • Retirement Accounts
    • Traditional IRA - tax deduction on contributions, and pay taxes when money is wdrawn later (about a/f 60yo)
    • Roth IRA - contribute money you've already paid taxes on but pay no taxes on wdrawals in retirement
    • 401k - similar to traditional IRA, can roll it into traditional IRA after you leave employer
      • Roth better deal than traditional b/c can contribute more to Roth (after tax worth more than pre-tax money) esp since you'll be in a higher tax bracket later
      • look at the fund offerings quality
      • if expense ratios >1% then it's a bad one --> only contribute up to the match
      • if expense ratio <0.5% and/or includes Vanguard's index funds or Fidelity's Spartan-class funds --> contribute in excess of match limits
  • How to Spend down money in retirement
    • purchase inflation-adjusted fixed annuity (similar to traditional pension plan, or TIPS)
Recommended Books
  • Millionaire Next Door
  • Common Sense Mutual Funds
  • Devil Take the Hindmost
  • The Great Depression
  • Your Money and Your Brain
  • How a Second Grader Beats Wall Street
  • All About Asset Allocation
 Definitions
  • Expense Ratio
    • % of assets used for administrative, management, advertising etc.
    • Ex: 1%/year = 1% funds assets will be used to cover expenses each year
    • Doesn't include sales loads or brokerage commissions
    • small funds tend to have higher ratios
    • Typical US domestic stock fund ~1%, but passively managed funds (index funds) lower ratios
  • Taxable Account
    • you pay taxes on investment income in the year it was received
    • Ex: individual and joint investment (savings) accounts, bank accounts, money market mutual funds (gov securities, T bills, CDs, commercial paper)
    • Make sure you declare investments that are taxable
    • Some investments are more tax-efficient than others
  • Non-taxable Account
    • Retirement accounts (401k, IRA). Interests earned is not taxed.
    • But can be Tax-deferred
      • Taxed when you withdraw money (ex 401k vs Roth IRA)
  • Mutual Fund Companies vs owners
    • investment made up of pools of funds (stocks, bonds, money market etc) operated by money managers
    • helpful for small investors - those who don't have enough money to diversify their portfolio. With other investors you pool money in to create wanted portfolio to create capital.
    • Shares = mutual fund units
    • Fund redeemed at fund's current Net Asset Value (NAV)
    • sometimes can get charged more in fees than expense ratio

item.title: The Millionaire Next Door (Stanley)
item.dc:creator: acoke4u
item.content:encoded:
Introduction 7 common denominators among the people who become wealthy
  1. They live well below their means
  2. They allocate their time and money efficiently, in ways conducive to building wealth. 
  3. They believe that financial independence is more important than displaying high social status. 
  4. Their parents did not provide economic outpatient care. 
  5. Their adult children are economically self-sufficient. 
  6. They are proficient in targeting market opportunities. 
  7. They chose the right occupation. 
Chapter 1: Meet the Millionaire Next Door 
  • What would the prototypical millionaire in American tell you about himself?
    • Many of the types of businesses we own are classified as dull-normal. We are welding contractors, auctioneers, rice farmers, pest controllers, and paving contractors.
    • About 80 percent of us are first-generation affluent.
    • We have accumulated enough wealth so we wouldn't have to work for ten or more years.
    • About two-thirds of us work between forty-five and fifty-five hours per week.
    • We are picky investors.
    • "I am my favorite charity."
  • The authors define wealthy as getting much more pleasure from owning substantial amounts of appreciable assets than from buying and owning many materials.
  • Net Worth Estimation: (=asset owned minus debt owed)
    • Target Net Worth = Age X Annual Pre-Tax Income / 10
    • Modified: Target Net Worth = (Age – 27) X Annual Pre-Tax Income / 5
Chapter 2: Frugal Frugal Frugal
  • Realized income = income actually received that can be used but also taxed (ex: salary, cashing out stock) <-- minimize this
  • Unrealized income = potential income that has not been cashed out and also not taxed (ex: house, investments etc) <-- maximize this
  • Average millionaire lives in middle-class home, does not buy lavish stuffs. Annual realized income is <7% of net worth (<7% weath is taxed)
  • Income tax is the single largest annual expenditure for most households, so maximize unrealized income. Some are poor b/c they maximize realized income (ex salary) so they can support lavish lifestyles (ex: 90% of their wealth is realized income vs <7% in millioniares)
  • General rule : never purchase a home that requires a mortgage that is more than twice your household's total annual realized income.
Chapter 3: Time, Energy, and Money
  • Distribute your time, energy and money to benefit your net worth via PLANNING and CONTROLLING regularly.
  • For ex: know family's budget/consumption and limits. Then will not need to be concerned about increasing tax, gov regulations/inflation etc..
Chapter 4: You Aren't What You Drive
  • Most millionaires buy cars <$30K. Consider buying used car since it quickly depreciates
Chapter 5: Economic Outpatient Care
  • Economic Outpatient Care (EOC) refers to the economic gifts and "acts of kindness" come parents give their adult children and grandchildren.
  • Essentially, don't spoil your kids, educate about building wealth and managing finances early.
Chapter 6: Affirmative Action, Family Style
Recommendations on how to raise financially successful kids:
  1. Never tell children their parents are wealthy.
  2. No matter how wealthy you are, teach your children discipline and frugality.
  3. Assure that your children won't realize you're affluent until after they have established a mature, disciplined, and adult lifestyle and profession.
  4. Minimize discussions of the items that each child and grandchild will inherit or receive as gifts.
  5. Never give cash or other significant gifts to your adult children as part of a negotiation strategy.
Chapter 7: Find Your Niche
  • The frugal of the wealthy are price-sensitive when it comes to many consumer products and services. They are not near as sensitive when it comes to purchasing advice and services, accounting services, tax advice and legal services. Since the majority of the affluent are self-employed business owners and managers, they are also buyers of industrial products and services.

item.title: In Search of A Meaningful Job
item.dc:creator: acoke4u
item.content:encoded:
Sometimes it's right in front of you, that perfect job. You're actually doing it right now, but being in the eye of the storm, you forget the impact you make in the world. It's interesting to see how our jobs have evolved after the industrial revolution and how our careers have become a separate entity from who we are. We cannot be boxed into a single role. We are more than our job description, filled with creativity and ideas. If your job does not ask for what you are made of, show them what you can achieve. Bring meaning to your job.

item.title: Westworld (quotes)
item.dc:creator: acoke4u
item.content:encoded:
Any man whose errors take ten years to correct is quite a man. - J. Robert Oppenheimer. (An American physicist who pioneered the development of the first nuclear weapons used during WWII. "Now I am become Death, the destroyer of worlds.")

I guess people want to read about the things they want the most and experience the least. -Bernard

I'm not crying for myself. I'm cryin' for you. They say that great beasts once roamed this world. Big as mountains. Yet all that's left of them is bone and amber. Time undoes even the mightiest creatures. Just look what it's done to you. One day, you will perish. You will like with the rest of your kind in the dirt. Your dreams forgotten, your horrors faced, your muscles will turn to sand, and upon that sand a new God will walk, one that will never die, because this world doesn't belong to you or the people who came before. It belongs to someone who is yet to come. - Dolores

My father used to say that only boring people get bored. - Ford

I've been pretending my whole life. Pretending I don't mind, pretending I belong. My life's built on it. And it's a good life; it's the life I've always wanted. But then I came here, and I get a glimpse for a second of a life in which I don't have to pretend, of a life in which I can be truly alive. How can I go back to pretending when I know what this feels like? - William

I used to think this place was all about pandering to your baser instincts. Now I understand It doesn't cater to your lower self, it reveals your deepest self; it shows you who you really are. - William

Host: You want to ask, so ask. William: Are you real? Host: Well, if you can't tell, does it matter?

Some people choose to see the ugliness in this world, the disarray. I choose to see the beauty. To believe there is an order to our days. A purpose. -Dolores

There is no threshold that makes us greater than the sum of our parts, no inflection point at which we become fully alive. We can't define consciousness because consciousness does not exist. Humans fancy that there's something special about the way we perceive the world, and yet we live in loops, as tight and as closed as the hosts do, seldom questioning our choices, content, for the most part, to be told what to do next. No, my friend, you're not missing anything at all. - Ford

I've told you, Bernard, never place your trust in us. We're only human. Inevitably, we'll only disappoint you. Goodbye my friend. - Ford

Good evening. Since I was a child... I always loved a good story. I believed that stories helped us to ennoble ourselves, to fix what was broken in us, and to help us become the people we dreamed of being. Lies that told a deeper truth. I always thought I could play some small part in the grand tradition. And for my pains... I got this. A prison of our own sins. 'Cause you don't want to change, or cannot change. Because you're only human after all. But then I realized someone was paying attention, someone who could change. So I began to compose a new story for them. It begins with the birth of a new people and the choices they will have to make. And the people, they will decide to become. And we'll have all those things that you have always enjoyed: surprises and violence. It begins in times of war, with a villain, named Wyatt. And a killing. This time by choice. I'm sad to say, this will be my last story. An old friend once told me something that gave me comfort. Something he had read. He said that Mozart, Beethoven and Chopin never died, they simply became music. So I hope you will enjoy this last piece... very much. - Ford

We humans are alone in this world for a reason. We've murdered and butchered anything that challenged our privacy. - Ford

Even I fell into the most terrible of human traps... Trying to change what is already past. - Ford

A greyhound is a racing dog. Spends its life running in circles, chasing a bit of felt made up like a rabbit. One day, we took it to the park. Our dad had warned us how fast that dog was, but we couldn't resist. So, my brother took off the leash, and in that instant, the dog spotted a cat. I imagine it must have looked just like that piece of felt. He ran. Never saw a thing as beautiful as that old dog running. Until, at last, he finally caught it. And to the horror of everyone, he killed that little cat. Tore it to pieces. Then he just sat there, confused. That dog had spent its whole life trying to catch that... thing. Now it had no idea what to do. - Ford

If you go looking for the truth, get the whole thing. It's like a good fuck. Half is worse than none at all. - Maeve

See, it took 500 years for someone to notice, something hidden in plain sight. A doctor, he noticed the shape of the human brain. The message being, that divine gift does not come from a higher power, but from our own minds. - Ford

Reference: The Creation of Adam (Michelangelo), Wikipedia.org

item.title: Do not go gentle into that good night (poem)
item.dc:creator: acoke4u
item.content:encoded:
by Dylan Thomas, 1914 - 1953

Do not go gentle into that good night, Old age should burn and rave at close of day; Rage, rage against the dying of the light. Though wise men at their end know dark is right, Because their words had forked no lightning they Do not go gentle into that good night. Good men, the last wave by, crying how bright Their frail deeds might have danced in a green bay, Rage, rage against the dying of the light. Wild men who caught and sang the sun in flight, And learn, too late, they grieved it on its way, Do not go gentle into that good night. Grave men, near death, who see with blinding sight Blind eyes could blaze like meteors and be gay, Rage, rage against the dying of the light. And you, my father, there on the sad height, Curse, bless, me now with your fierce tears, I pray. Do not go gentle into that good night. Rage, rage against the dying of the light.

item.title: CGM
item.dc:creator: acoke4u
item.content:encoded:
Recent few months I've been exploring fitness and health. The information out there is massive and you've really got to deep dive into the literature to simplify and find what ways work for you. Here I wanted to briefly write about the CGM experience.

CGM (continuous glucose monitoring)
This was both a fun and stressful experience. I went deep into the glucose literature and have learned that in general glucose spikes, glucose fluctuations, and high glucose baselines are in generally bad. It causes inflammation with the spikes and glycogenating your cells just makes it age faster. And the less fluctuations/spikes and lower glucose baseline levels the better.

What I've learned is that:

  • CGM is quite a useful tool as an accountability coach. When you become obsessed with seeing how your glucose changes after you eat something, you feel guilty eating carbs and sugars that tend to spike it more.
  • I've learned that I could try to avoid sugar and complex carbs.
  • Eating fiber (vegies etc) and vinegar will help attenuate those spikes
  • Mixing fats can also do this, but then you have to watch your cholesterol / calories - there's always a give and take
  • Eating only 80% full, or making sure you're hungry before you eat really helped control the glucose. I didn't realize I kept on eating when I really didn't need to. Still not sure if grazing is better or having timed meals would be.
  • I was obsessing with veggies and protein for awhile, but then started to get protein spilling out of my urine and flank pain. I am now in the boat of eat what you use. Carbs is not bad if you use it especially if you are doing alot of cardio (zone 2). Protein is helpful if you're building muscles, but otherwise it can be hard on your kidneys if the excess if excreted in large amounts. There's some vague literature that might even show too much protein can be harmful as well but jury is still out depending on who you ask.
  • I was meal prepping most of my food, and that took waaay too much of my time.
  • Having the monitor on was uncomfortable since it does puncture your skin. Not that you feel it but the device itself does hinder my workout swim routines. Also, readings were inconsistent depending on if I put it on my arm vs abdomen. (used dexcom 7)
  • My life revolved around controlling it that I don't think I enjoyed food at all, but it did help me be more conscious about what I'm eating.

I will continue to try the CGM occasionally to see if I've been able to improve my levels. There will soon be a noninvasive CGM in the next few years so will definitely be more likely to have that around. For now, moving on to the next longevity fad.
